title: Merchant Velocity — outbound opportunity journal
content:
Quick context:
- Prospect: Merchant Velocity (mid-market marketplace for specialty retailers). Headcount ~220, Series B, heavy on catalog ops and merchant analytics.
- Why interesting: heavy reliance on human-curated product copy and manual merchant onboarding flows; reported 27% drop in conversion for new SKUs month 1 (public pitch deck). Potential to upsell platform value via better product discovery, auto-generated copy, and chat support for merchants.
- Intro source: intro from Alina (channel partner) — met with Head of Ops (Samir) 2025-02-07 (30m).

Notes from 2025-02-07 call (Samir, Head of Ops; Lena, Dir. Product):
- Pain: onboarding/taxonomy mismatch across merchant feeds; large backlog of product descriptions and missing specs.
- Current infra: internal microservices + hosted search (Algolia). They run nightly batch jobs for attribute normalization; content team of 6 writers.
- Primary use cases they sounded open to:
  - Auto-generate 2–3 short product descriptions + seo-friendly headline per SKU (goal: reduce time-to-live for new listings)
  - Conversational merchant assistant (chat) to help merchants fix feed errors and tag attributes (reduce support tickets)
  - Embedding-based product discovery (semantic search reranking) to improve new-SKU findability
- Constraints/reqs:
  - Data privacy: want assurance PII not retained. Interested in Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC and KMS integration. Mentioned legal/regulatory customers in EU.
  - Latency: user-facing merchant chat target ~200–300ms avg generation for short replies.
  - Cost sensitivity: narrow margins; will evaluate unit economics closely — need predictable pricing or reserved capacity.
- Decision timeline: looking at pilots Q2, vendor selection by end of Q2.

Technical notes & rough Sizing (quick calc):
- Estimated traffic for merchant chat pilot: 200 concurrent merchant sessions, avg 1.2 requests/min per session during business hours => ~240 qps? Wait — re-calc: 200 sessions * 1.2 / 60 = 4 qps. Good catch, initial pilot ~4 qps, peak bursts up to 15 qps.
- Product description generation: assume 10k new SKUs/week for pilot-catalog subset. Each description ~120 tokens output + 80 token prompt => ~200 tokens per generation. If we do 3 variants per SKU => 600 tokens * 10k/week = 6M tokens/week.
- Implication: hosted per-token costs add up; Dedicated or Reserved pool likely needed for predictable unit economics.

Objections we should be ready for + suggested responses:
1) "We can't send product/merchant PII to a third-party"
   - Response: Redwood Private can be deployed into their VPC or on-prem (air-gapped), plus we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and explicit data retention policies. Offer SOC2 + logs for audit.
2) "Latency — our merchant UX will break if model is slow"
   - Response: Emphasize Redwood's serving runtime (GPU-optimized, batching controls, prefix caching). Propose small canary with 99th percentile target and automated fallback to a lightweight template generator. Show latency benchmarks for similar workloads (attach later).
3) "Cost — we're price sensitive and want predictable pricing"
   - Response: Recommend Redwood Dedicated with reserved commit to smooth unit costs; also propose hybrid: Dedicated for chat + hosted for non-sensitive bulk generation until pilot scales. We can provide an expected cost model for pilot (TCO sheet).
4) "Quality control — writers will resist generated copy"
   - Response: Position Redwood Optimize + evals: run A/B tests with writers in the loop, provide generation settings and safety nets (temperature, n-best reranking), and keep writer editorial control (approve/publish flow).

Outbound email drafts (cold intro -> short, then follow up):
- Cold intro (to Samir/Lena style):
  Subject: Cut listing time for new merchants by 50% (pilot idea)
  Hi Samir —
  Quick note — saw Merchant Velocity's focus on onboarding speed and high-volume catalogs. We helped a marketplace reduce new-SKU publish time by ~60% with automated descriptions + semantic search. Could I share a 4-week pilot plan that: (1) auto-generates descriptions for a subset of SKUs, (2) runs an A/B with your writer team, (3) integrates with Algolia for reranking? 15 min to review?
  — Maya

- Follow-up 5 days later:
  Subject: pilot plan + quick cost estimate
  Samir —
  Following up on pilot idea. Attached: one-pager + expected token consumption and two pricing options (hosted vs dedicated pilot). If helpful, we can do a tech sync with your infra lead + sample dataset upload checklist.

Call script for intro demo (10–15m):
- 0–3m: quick problem recap (we listened)
- 3–6m: 2 min demo: auto-describe 3 sample SKUs (show 2 variations + metadata extraction)
- 6–10m: discuss infra / privacy needs, timeline, success criteria (CTR for discovery, publish time, writer acceptance rate)
- 10–15m: next steps: pilot scope, POC data access, security questionnaire

Next steps / TODOs (who):
- [Maya] send tailored one-pager + pilot cost estimate (due 2025-02-12)
- [Rafael] prep short benchmark note comparing avg latency for chat on gpt-ish vs small local 8-bit quantized models (due 2025-02-17)
- [Priya] create dataset checklist for merchant feed anonymization + sample upload (due 2025-02-14)
- Request tech sync: target Samir + Lena + infra lead (1 hr) — propose 2025-02-20 or 21.

Potential upsells / longer-term value hooks:
- Full on-prem deployment for EU customers (compliance)
- Embeddings + semantic search product discovery to complement Algolia — upsell to subscription pricing tied to index size
- Template-based dynamic pricing hints (advanced feature)

Open questions (to resolve before pilot scope):
- Are there any specific fields in merchant feeds considered 'sensitive' beyond contact emails? (Samir to confirm.)
- Exact SLA requirement for merchant chat 99th percentile — they mentioned 200–300ms but need baseline measurement.
- Who owns Algolia integration on their side? (infra or frontend)

Random scratch thoughts / short-term experiments:
- Could run a tiny writer-in-the-loop test: 100 SKUs -> 3 gen variants -> writers rate 1–5. If median >=4, move to 2k SKUs.
- Consider shipping pre-built Algolia reranker plugin as a quick win (low integration cost).
